subject: Clarify token-flooring across long chat history and split-session invoicing
messages:
From: Maya Chen <maya@cartly.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Finance Ops <billing@cartly.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Sep 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on token accounting for long histories + invoice examples

Hi Tessa / Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. We're almost ready to sign but Finance has two closely related asks before we finalize the SOW: how you (1) bill when a single user conversation exceeds the model context window and is split into two inference calls (historical tokens moved to a short-term store), and (2) how the monthly minimums/rounding interact with those split calls.

Specific example they asked for (approx):
- Single user session across one day with 6,400 tokens of history + 1,200 new tokens in the latest message. Our standard model context = 4,096 tokens.
- When you drop the oldest history to keep the latest 4,096 tokens in the live context, what shows on our invoice? Do we get charged for: 
  a) 6,400 + 1,200 = 7,600 tokens total (full session), or 
  b) two separate calls (4,096 + 3,504 + 1,200) with rounding/minimums applied per-call, or 
  c) some hybrid where prefix reuse is credited?

They also want to understand how our committed floor (we're looking at the 3M token/month floor in the draft) changes the math if you do per-call rounding (e.g., 100-token quantum rounding).

Can you send an invoice-style sample with both the strict per-call approach and the prefix-credit approach? If possible, highlight where rounding causes visible delta and what concessions (if any) Redwood would offer in a committed-floor deal.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our procurement has a Friday deadline.

Best,
Maya
Director of Product, Cartly
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Chen <maya@cartly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Finance Ops <billing@cartly.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Oct 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on token accounting for long histories + invoice examples

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the concrete example, that helps a lot. I've attached two artifacts: a short PDF (redwood_token_rounding_examples.pdf) that explains our canonical billing rules, and a worked spreadsheet (Cartly_Billing_Sample.xlsx) with the two invoice scenarios you requested. Quick summary below, then the attachments and next steps.

High-level answers (short):
- We meter each inference call at the time it executes. That means an initial full-context call is billed for the tokens actually processed on that call. If the server trims old history and the client issues a subsequent call, that subsequent call is billed for the tokens included in that second request. There is no automatic retroactive "session-level" aggregation unless you opt into a committed-floor reconciliation.
- Rounding / minimums are applied at the invoice line level. For hosted customers without a committed floor: per-call token counts are consolidated into usage buckets and then rounded according to the published quantum (100-token units). That can cause small deltas when many split calls occur.
- With a committed floor (your 3M token/month example), we run a monthly reconciliation: your usage is tallied post-rounding, and if it falls under the floor we invoice the committed amount; if it exceeds, overage is billed at the agreed rate. We can offer a prefix-reuse credit option for long-history conversational workloads under dedicated agreements — this is an explicit concession, not default behavior.

In the attached spreadsheet I've modeled your numbers both ways:
- Sheet A: Strict per-call billing (calls created by trimming the history) with 100-token rounding applied per-call.
- Sheet B: Committed-floor reconciliation with a 3M token floor and a negotiated 5% prefix-reuse credit applied to qualifying session tokens.

Next steps: if you can confirm which model you prefer (strict per-call vs committed-floor with prefix credit), we'll produce a one-page SOW addendum that codifies the crediting rule and the exact rounding quantum.

Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

—Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Oct 2028 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: internal: suggested concession language for Cartly (prefix reuse + rounding)

Tessa —

Drafted a short concession we can offer to Cartly to keep the deal moving and limit revenue downside from heavy-history churn:

1) Prefix-reuse credit: For qualifying conversational sessions where >50% of tokens in a rolling 30-day session are repeated prefixes (detectable via stable session id), Redwood will apply a 5% credit to billable tokens associated with that session. Credit applies only to hosted deals with a committed floor >= 1M tokens/month and requires a 90-day pilot evaluation.

2) Rounding quantum: Maintain standard 100-token rounding for metering. For customers on committed floors we will perform invoice-level rounding reconciliation (aggregate first, round second) to reduce per-call rounding overheads.

3) Example calculation language (for SOW): "Billable tokens are computed as the sum of tokens processed by the inference runtime during the billing period. For committed-floor customers, Redwood will aggregate raw token usage across the billing period, apply contractual credits (e.g., prefix-reuse), and then apply quantum rounding to the aggregated total prior to invoicing."

If you want more generous credits we can tier to 10% at a 5M token floor, but let's see Cartly's comfort level first.

Ben
Director, Revenue Operations

On a side note, attaching sample calc I ran against Maya's numbers (same spreadsheet). If they push on the 100-token quantum being unfair, propose the aggregation-first rounding approach in the SOW — it preserves us while materially lowering rounding leakage for them.
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Question on token accounting for long histories + invoice examples

Maya / Raj —

Thanks again for the patience while we modeled this. I've attached the two files Ben mentioned; below is the plain-language summary you can include with procurement.

Plain-language summary (what will appear in the SOW if you accept):
- Metering: Redwood bills tokens processed by the model at call time. For hosted customers with no floor, rounding occurs at invoice-line consolidation (per-call buckets are summed then rounded).
- Committed-floor reconciliation: For customers that sign a committed floor, Redwood will aggregate raw usage over the month, apply contractual credits, then round the final aggregated total prior to invoicing (this reduces rounding noise).
- Prefix-reuse credit (proposed concession): For qualifying conversational workloads we will apply a 5% credit to qualifying session tokens after aggregation. Qualification requires a session id signal and an initial 90-day pilot to validate patterns.

Practical example (from your numbers):
- If Cartly runs the 7,600 token session you described and sessions are billed strictly as executed calls, you will see ~7,600 tokens of raw usage. Under per-call rounding you may pay an additional ~100–200 tokens due to quantum rounding depending on how many calls are created.
- If Cartly signs the 3M committed floor + accepts the 5% prefix credit and we do aggregation-first rounding, the same workload will be aggregated, 5% credit applied to qualifying tokens, then rounded once — your invoice delta drops materially.

Requested action: please confirm by EOD Friday whether you want the SOW addendum to include the 5% prefix-reuse credit and aggregation-first rounding. If yes, we'll draft the one-paragraph addendum and route for signature.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call Thursday if helpful.

Best,
Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
